questions.question: Which act replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973?
questions.solution: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the colonial-era Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.

questions.question: As per the Constitution (Ninety-First Amendment) Act, 2003, the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall NOT exceed:
questions.option_1: 20% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.option_2: 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.option_3: 10% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.option_4: 25% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha
questions.solution: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 restricted the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha (or Legislative Assembly for states).

questions.question: Part IV A of the Indian Constitution was inserted through which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.solution: Part IV-A, which lists the Fundamental Duties, was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 based on the Swaran Singh Committee recommendations.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act:
1. It introduced 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS).
2. It amended Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The 103rd Amendment Act (2019) provided 10% reservation for EWS by inserting Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

questions.question: The 42nd Amendment of the Indian Constitution (1976) added which of the following terms to the Preamble?
questions.solution: The 42nd Amendment Act amended the Preamble to include three new words: Socialist, Secular, and Integrity.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 mandated a 3-tier Panchayati Raj system for all states having a population above 20 lakh.
2. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee first recommended the three-tier structure consisting of Zilla Parishad, Panchayat Samiti, and Gram Panchayat.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. The 73rd Amendment established a uniform three-tier system (Gram, Intermediate/Block, and District levels), but states with a population under 20 lakh may not constitute the intermediate level. The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (1957) was the first to recommend this 'Democratic Decentralisation' structure.

questions.question: In which year did the 44th Amendment remove the right to property from the list of fundamental rights?
questions.solution: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 removed the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right (Article 31) and made it a legal/constitutional right under Article 300A in Part XII.

questions.question: Which among the following is INCORRECT about the salient features of the 73rd Amendment Act?
questions.option_1: The Act corresponds to Part III of the Constitution of India.
questions.option_2: The Act gives a Constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj Institutions.
questions.option_3: The Act has added the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution of India.
questions.option_4: It contains 29 functional items of the Panchayats and deals with Article 243 to 243(O).
questions.solution: Option (a) is incorrect. The 73rd Amendment Act added Part IX (not Part III) to the Constitution. Part III contains Fundamental Rights.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. As per Article 368, the Indian Constitution provides for two types of amendment procedures.
2. Certain amendments require not only a special majority in Parliament but also ratification by at least half of the state legislatures.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Article 368 specifies two types of amendments: by a special majority of Parliament, and by a special majority plus ratification by half of the states (for federal provisions). Note that simple majority amendments fall outside the scope of Article 368.

questions.question: Which among the following Constitutional Amendment Act reduced the age of voting from 21 to 18 for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.solution: The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (which came into force in 1989) reduced the voting age from 21 to 18 by amending Article 326.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 71st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages in the Eighth Schedule.
2. The 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali languages, raising the total to 22.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali (KMN) were added in 1992. Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (BDMS) were added in 2003, bringing the total number of languages in the 8th Schedule to 22.

questions.question: The Eighty-ninth Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution established which of the following Commission?
questions.solution: The 89th Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the erstwhile combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate bodies: National Commission for Scheduled Castes (Art 338) and National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Art 338A).

questions.question: Which of the following Amendments of the Constitution of India gave the status of state to Goa?
questions.solution: The 56th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1987 conferred statehood on Goa and made Daman and Diu a separate Union Territory.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India abolished the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states?
questions.solution: The 26th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971 abolished the privy purses (annual payments) and special privileges previously granted to the former rulers of princely states.

questions.question:
Arrange the following Fundamental Rights in the order they are listed in the Indian Constitution:
1. Right to Constitutional Remedies
2. Right to Freedom
3. Right against Exploitation
4. Right to Equality
questions.solution: The correct sequence is: Right to Equality (Art 14-18), Right to Freedom (Art 19-22), Right against Exploitation (Art 23-24), and Right to Constitutional Remedies (Art 32). Thus, 4-2-3-1.

questions.question: Which of the following duties is specified as the 10th Fundamental Duty in the Indian Constitution?
questions.option_1: To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
questions.option_2: To provide opportunities for education to his child between 6 and 14 years
questions.option_3: To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle
questions.option_4: To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry
questions.solution: The 10th Fundamental Duty (Art 51A(j)) is 'to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity'. The 11th duty (education) was added later by the 86th Amendment.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding writ jurisdiction in India:
1. Only the Supreme Court can issue writs under Article 32.
2. High Courts are empowered to issue writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights as well as for other purposes under Article 226.
3. The Constitution of India recognizes five types of writs.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: All statements are correct. Article 32 is for the Supreme Court to protect FRs. Article 226 gives High Courts wider power to issue writs for FRs and other legal rights. There are five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution prohibits providing of any religious instruction in the educational institutions maintained by the State?
questions.solution: Article 28 states that no religious instruction shall be provided in any educational institution wholly maintained out of State funds.

questions.question: If a 12-year-old is found to be working in a factory manufacturing carpets, which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India will be violated?
questions.solution: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous employment.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Writ of Mandamus in the Indian Constitution:
1. The Writ of Mandamus compels a public authority to perform a duty it is bound to do.
2. It is available under the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32 and 226).
3. It is classified under the Right to Equality in the Constitution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Writ of Mandamus is a judicial remedy issued to direct a public authority to perform its legal duties. It falls under the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Articles 32 for the Supreme Court and 226 for High Courts). Statement 3 is incorrect because it is not part of the Right to Equality (Articles 14-18).

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 20 of the Indian Constitution:
1. Clause (2) of Article 20 embodies the doctrine of Double Jeopardy.
2. Double Jeopardy means that no person shall be prosecuted and punished more than once for the same offence.
3. The doctrine of Double Jeopardy is contained in Article 20(3) of the Constitution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 20(2) specifically contains the doctrine of Double Jeopardy, which protects a person from being punished more than once for the same offence. Statement 3 is incorrect because Article 20(3) refers to protection against self-incrimination (being forced to be a witness against oneself).

questions.question: Article 20 of the Constitution of India is related to _____.
questions.option_1: equality of opportunities in matters of public employment
questions.option_2: protection in respect of conviction for offenses
questions.solution: Article 20 provides protection to individuals accused of crimes through three main principles: Ex-Post Facto Laws (no retrospective punishment), Double Jeopardy (no double punishment), and Self-Incrimination (right to remain silent).

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution states that ‘It shall be the duty of every citizen of India to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India transcending religious, linguistic and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.’?
questions.solution: This specific provision is listed as Article 51A (e) under the Fundamental Duties. It aims to foster unity and respect for women among all citizens.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Constitutional Remedies:
1. Dr. B.R. Ambedkar described the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32) as the “Heart and Soul of the Constitution.”
2. Article 32 empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
3. The Right to Constitutional Remedies was called the “Soul of the Constitution” by Jawaharlal Nehru during the Constituent Assembly debates.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 32 allows citizens to move the Supreme Court to protect their rights via writs. Dr. Ambedkar famously called it the 'Heart and Soul' because it makes all other rights meaningful. Statement 3 is incorrect as the quote is attributed to Dr. Ambedkar, not Nehru.

questions.question: Certiorari comes under the:
questions.solution: Certiorari is one of the five writs available under the Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32). It is issued to quash the order of a lower court or tribunal.
